# Quickstart: Core Entry Workflow (SPEC-0006)

**Date**: 2026-08-14 | **Spec**: [SPEC-0006](spec.md) | **Entries API**:
[contracts/entries-api.md](contracts/entries-api.md) | **Data model**:
[data-model.md](data-model.md) | **Research**: [research.md](research.md)

This guide validates the Phase 1 core entry workflow end-to-end. It is a
**run/validation guide** — implementation details live in `tasks.md` (regenerated by
`/speckit.tasks`) and the implementation phase.

## 1. Prerequisites

- SQL Server with the legacy `VisaEntry` database (read-only) and the migrated target
  `VisaFusion` database (SPEC-0004 delivered the 38-entity schema + identity import).
- .NET 8 SDK; the `VisaFusion.sln` solution builds (`dotnet build`).
- Configuration (connection strings, `Jwt:*` key) via `appsettings.json` / User
  Secrets — no secrets in source; `ProductionSecretsGuard` fails fast in Production
  with dev-only config.
- For the stored-proc integration tests: write access to a disposable test copy of the
  target `VisaFusion` database (per the existing integration-test convention — tests
  self-skip when SQL Server is unreachable).

## 2. Setup

```text
dotnet restore
dotnet build VisaFusion.sln
# Pre-cutover: verify every `-- TODO: confirm column name` in the owner-supplied
# scripts against the live schema (sp_help / INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS) — GR-0001 caveat.
# Execute the owner-supplied scripts in order at cutover (01-08):
sqlcmd -S <server> -d VisaFusion -i specs/006-core-entry-workflow/scripts/01_sequences_and_allocation.sql
sqlcmd -S <server> -d VisaFusion -i specs/006-core-entry-workflow/scripts/02_fn_IsEmbassyClosed.sql
sqlcmd -S <server> -d VisaFusion -i specs/006-core-entry-workflow/scripts/03_report_procedures.sql
sqlcmd -S <server> -d VisaFusion -i specs/006-core-entry-workflow/scripts/04_migration_cleansing_procedures.sql
sqlcmd -S <server> -d VisaFusion -i specs/006-core-entry-workflow/scripts/05_normalization_ddl.sql
sqlcmd -S <server> -d VisaFusion -i specs/006-core-entry-workflow/scripts/06_status_change_and_superuser_provisioning.sql
sqlcmd -S <server> -d VisaFusion -i specs/006-core-entry-workflow/scripts/07_gr0004_corrected_entry_status_change.sql
sqlcmd -S <server> -d VisaFusion -i specs/006-core-entry-workflow/scripts/08_finalize_entry_status_change_updatedby.sql
dotnet run --project src/VisaFusion.Web
```

Note: scripts 07 and 08 both `CREATE OR ALTER dbo.usp_RecordEntryStatusChange`; 08
supersedes 07 (GR-0004) — running both in order leaves the final (08) definition in
place.

## 3. Validation Scenarios (map to spec §23 Test Scenarios)

| Scenario | Command / check | Expected outcome |
|----------|-----------------|------------------|
| Refno allocation (AC-003) | Integration test: call `usp_AllocateNextRefno` concurrently (e.g. 50 parallel calls) | Unique, monotonic max+1 values; no duplicates, no collisions; gaps permitted (BR-001) |
| Status change atomicity (AC-004) | Integration test: `usp_RecordEntryStatusChange` with valid refno/paxId/countryId/newStatusId + `@ActorUserId` | `PaxStatus.statusID` updated AND `StatusHistory` + `bighistory` rows written in one commit; `@NewStatusHistoryId` returned; `UpdatedBy` = `{role}:{username}` (GR-0004) |
| Status change rollback | Integration test: force an error mid-proc (e.g. nonexistent status id) | `RAISERROR`; no partial writes — `PaxStatus` unchanged, no orphan history rows (XACT_ABORT) |
| Bookable-date rule (AC-005) | Unit test: `HolidayService` for holiday / weekly-off / Sunday / normal day; integration test: `fn_IsEmbassyClosed` for the same dates | Both return 1 for holiday/weekly-off/Sunday, 0 otherwise — rule parity (FR-006/BR-003) |
| Super-user provisioning (AC-006) | Integration test: `usp_ProvisionSuperUser` (pre-hashed password) | `su` user created with `su`+`adm` roles; `SuperUserProvisioningAudit` row written; duplicate username refused; non-su caller rejected (proc-level) |
| Create entry (AC-007) | `POST /api/v1/entries` with a valid payload (JWT for emp/adm/su) | `201` with allocated `refno` + `etag`; entry + passenger persisted |
| Get entry | `GET /api/v1/entries/{refno}` | `200` with entry, passengers, paxStatuses, `etag`; unknown refno → `404` |
| Optimistic concurrency (AC-011) | `PUT /api/v1/entries/{refno}` with a stale `If-Match` ETag; then with a fresh ETag | Stale → `409` (problem-details); fresh → `200` with new `etag` |
| Status endpoint | `POST /api/v1/entries/{refno}/status` (valid status id) | `200` with `statusHistoryId` + `updatedBy`; nonexistent status id → `400` |
| Sent-AWB | `POST /api/v1/entries/{refno}/awb` | `204`; unknown refno → `404` |
| RBAC matrix (AC-008) | Hermetic functional test over all 5 Entries endpoints | Anonymous → `401`; wrong role (agt/guest) → `403`; correct role (emp/adm/su) → `200`/`201`/`204` |
| Deferred superuser route | `POST /api/v1/admin/superusers` | Route does NOT exist (404) — documented-only contract (spec §15; `secured-write-routes.md` §3.1) |
| SQLi regression | Raw `'` inputs against the Entries endpoints | Parameterized — no injection (NFR-003) |
| Golden-file parity | Sanitized subset diff of entry create/status-change behavior | Old vs new behavior matches (where applicable, per migration plan §10) |

## 4. Automated Tests

```bash
dotnet test tests/UnitTests        # Entry aggregate invariants, HolidayService rule, refno allocation logic
dotnet test tests/FunctionalTests  # hermetic RBAC matrix + problem-details + optimistic-concurrency tests
dotnet test tests/IntegrationTests # stored-proc execution + atomicity + audit rows (self-skip without SQL Server)
```

All tests must pass before the feature is complete (constitution Principle V). The
Phase 1 exit criterion — "data model migrated, stored procs/functions live, Entries
API exposed under `/api/v1` with Phase-0 policies" (`library/ExecutionPlan.md` Phase 1,
items 4-6) — is proven by the scenarios above.

## 5. Security Spot-Checks

- No plaintext password material in logs, responses, or the super-user provisioning
  surface (NFR-006; password passed pre-hashed to `usp_ProvisionSuperUser`).
- `@ActorUserId` is resolved server-side from the JWT `sub` claim — never a
  caller-supplied formatted actor string (anti-spoofing, GR-0004).
- All write endpoints enforce the `EntryOperations` policy (401/403 as appropriate);
  the deferred superuser route is not registered (no anonymous write surface).
- All queries parameterized; no string-concatenated SQL (spec §12).
